result.title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin
result.summary: Attribution graphs over the features of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are used to predict what an ablation does and are compared across training seeds. A TopK SAE keeps the largest preactivations at each token, and a feature's margin is its preactivation's distance to the cutoff. On five public TopK SAE pairs from three Pythia models, zeroing one feature moves a next layer feature across the cutoff in 0.74 of cases or more, and the crossings carry most of the response's energy. Over writes that scale a feature's code by three factors, the graph built on the features active beforehand has a median relative error of 0.247 or more. The margin graph adds the first order change to every preactivation and reranks, at the same cost, and errs by at most 0.033. At the median, the crossing features' decoded change is 1.24 times the model's own change in norm or more. Between seeds of one testbed, sparse maps between features explain 0.85 of a graph's energy on its active features, and 0.47 once the other seed's graph keeps only its own. The largest model studied is pythia-160m.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 TopK SAE 上特征归因图在消融和跨种子比较中的可靠性，指出预激活到截断阈值的 margin 决定了特征跨越、从而主导响应，并提出以同成本的一阶 margin graph 重排序来修正误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 对稀疏特征归因中阈值边界效应的量化与修正，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent／特征级贡献分配与视觉证据筛选的归因稳健性，但目前仅限 Pythia 小模型与语言特征，迁移到多模态推理需验证。
